scope.boundaries: Public professional sources only. LinkedIn was used read-only through public indexed pages and exact-name results. No interaction, profile traversal, contact enrichment, or commercial search was used.

scoring_contract.active_gate_requirement: Confirmed identity, Saudi-market relevance, buying authority, plausible custom-software need, and at least one primary source.
scoring_contract.a_b_evidence_requirement: Two independent sources, including at least one primary or official source.
scoring_contract.unknown_capacity_rule: Unknown technical delivery capacity is neither a positive signal nor a penalty.

promoted.name: Shatha Khalid Alharbi | شذى الحربي
promoted.product_stage: Pre-company education project; progressed from a Saudi hackathon concept into Misk Launchpad 9 phase two for product refinement and prototype building
promoted.technical_capacity: Shatha is a computer-engineering student and has built technical projects, but the public evidence does not establish whether Suhail has a complete internal delivery team. Capacity is therefore unknown rather than scored positively or negatively.
observed_behaviour: Co-created and iterated an AI-personalized education platform from a Saudi hackathon project
Published a detailed first-person product narrative naming the founding collaborators and the specific learner and instructor workflows
Advanced the project into the second phase of Misk Launchpad 9

confirmed_identity.reason: The exact public profile identifies Shatha in Al-Qassim and contains her first-person Suhail project history.

saudi_market_basis.reason: The project originated in a hackathon run by Imam Abdulrahman Bin Faisal University and a Saudi AI-governance association, while Shatha is based in Al-Qassim. Misk independently describes Launchpad as a Saudi-focused pre-accelerator requiring founders to test and launch in the Kingdom.

buying_authority.reason: Shatha describes forming and developing the original project team, leading the idea's reframing into Suhail, and names the other co-founders and collaborators. This is direct founding-team product authority, not attendance alone.

plausible_custom_software_need.reason: Suhail is specified as an AI education platform that analyzes learning patterns, dynamically adapts content, generates personalized paths, and provides instructors with data-backed decisions.

has_primary_source.reason: A founder-team first-person source and the official Misk program page are present.

product_intent.reason: Within the last twelve months, Shatha described a specific AI platform, its user problem, feature set, founding team, and progression into phase two of a pre-accelerator.

outsourcing_likelihood.reason: The project has technical founders, but the evidence does not establish either sufficient delivery capacity or an external-builder search. Capacity remains unknown.

budget_readiness.reason: The team advanced through a structured Saudi pre-accelerator that provides MVP development and investment-readiness support; no cash software budget or secured funding is claimed.

timing.reason: The product narrative is approximately eight months old and the later cohort-completion update is approximately six months old. The project is monitor-worthy, but there is no fresher product-build milestone.

penalties.reason: No evidence-backed penalty applies. Profile silence after the cohort is not treated as proof of inactivity.

source_independence.note: The record is C-band, so the A/B two-independent-source rule does not apply. The official program page corroborates the cohort's Saudi and pre-company context but is not used to infer Shatha's authority.

evidence.source_title: Shatha Khalid Alharbi - Suhail project and Misk Launchpad 9 activity
evidence.paraphrased_evidence: Shatha's exact public profile places her in Al-Qassim and includes a first-person account of forming the project team in a Saudi university and AI-governance hackathon, evolving the initial Manhal concept into Suhail, specifying an AI-personalized learning platform, naming co-founders Ghadah Almutairi and Nada Alharbi, and advancing to Misk Launchpad 9 phase two. The profile also lists Suhail as a project with concrete AI and adaptive-learning capabilities.

Misk defines Launchpad as a Saudi-focused pre-accelerator for idea, prototype, and MVP-stage technology ventures. Its second phase is dedicated to developing a functional MVP, and admission requires Saudi founders or non-Saudis committed to testing and launching in Saudi Arabia.

Continuing would weaken the evidence rules or duplicate adjacent new-founder records.

limitations: Public LinkedIn indexing sometimes hides experience titles and job posters; hidden fields were not inferred.
No logged-in navigation, commercial search, browser extension, automated profile traversal, interaction, or contact-detail collection was used.
Relative LinkedIn ages were recorded with published_at null because no exact publication date was exposed.
Program participation corroborates stage and Saudi commitment only when combined with a founder-controlled product source; attendance alone was never used as qualification evidence.
